{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicate patient_ids
duplicate_patients = df['patient_id'].duplicated(keep=False)
dup_count = duplicate_patients.sum()

# Identify which patients are duplicated
duplicate_patients_list = df.loc[duplicate_patients, 'patient_id'].unique()

# Check sample_seq for each duplicate patient to see if higher sample_seq exists
# Keep only the row with the highest sample_seq per patient
# First, verify that sample_seq is numeric and not missing
assert df['sample_seq'].notna().all(), "sample_seq has missing values"

# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq descending, then drop duplicates on patient_id
# Keep the highest sample_seq row for each patient
df_clean = df.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False]).drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Confirm deduplication worked: should now have unique patient_id
assert df_clean['patient_id'].nunique() == df_clean.shape[0], "deduplication failed: still have duplicate patient_ids"

# Now, check assay_batch: batch B is in µg/L, must convert to ng/mL (1 µg/L = 10 ng/mL)
# So divide batch B's biomarker_final by 10
# Batch A is already in ng/mL

# Apply unit correction: batch B values are 10× too large
# Create a new column for corrected biomarker_final
# But since we're only interested in the final mean, we can do the correction in-place
# Note: The data dictionary says the unit error applies only to the week-12 assay (biomarker_final)
# So we only correct biomarker_final, not baseline

# Check that assay_batch is only 'A' or 'B'
assert set(df_clean['assay_batch'].unique()) == {'A', 'B'}, "assay_batch has unexpected values"

# Apply correction: divide biomarker_final by 10 for batch B
# Use .loc to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning
mask_batch_b = df_clean['assay_batch'] == 'B'

# Check if any biomarker_final values are -999 (baseline is the only one with sentinel)
# But just to be safe, check biomarker_final for -999
assert not (df_clean['biomarker_final'] == -999).any(), "biomarker_final contains -999, which is not expected"

# Correct the values
if mask_batch_b.any():
    df_clean.loc[mask_batch_b, 'biomarker_final'] /= 10

# Now compute the mean of biomarker_final in ng/mL
mean_biomarker_final = df_clean['biomarker_final'].mean()

print(f'Number of patients after deduplication: {df_clean.shape[0]}')
print(f'Mean biomarker_final (corrected to ng/mL): {mean_biomarker_final}')"}
